posts.title: Forum for posting comments on week 3-4 readings (due Oct 5)

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
How to make orderly observations

   In this chapter the author give us a big picture about how to make orderly observations for psychologists, or for all people interesting in human behavior. How to scientifically collect and analyze data to support our hypothesis and get rid of pitfalls and bias. The author addresses two main different approaches toward observation and data collection, one is the quantitative design, the other is qualitative design. Each approaches are then further described in detail, with many practical methods as well as each method’s pros and cons.

    At the end of the chapter, the author state that psychologists supporting quantitative design and the counterpart supporting qualitative design have an ongoing debate and seems like they've never agree with each other thus far. Which is quite interesting for me to think about which side I am. So here I’m going to share my opinion.

    I believed in numbers in the past. I thought only the quantitative data and repeatable experiments can a theory be proven. 

    The changes of my point came this summer, when I got a chance to help in I-Ju’s project. I got involved in an open-coding job, to add tags(codes) to wordy description by the respondents of questionnaires. I started to think maybe quantitative design isn’t the best way to represent these feelings, there are too many kind of circumstances and feelings that if we want to list it all, it would just be unpractical and cannot be represented again. So if theres infinite number of variables that we can not control, maybe the best way it to let it be, and we just try to catch as many information as possible. Which meets part of the ideas of qualitative design theory addressed by the author. So now I think if it’s possible to do the experiment than do it, but if not, sometimes qualitative design is a more clever and creative way to do the research.

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
Martin_Chapter 2_How to do experiments

 

This chapter has helped me to understand more about the variables that are used to measure and assess the experiment. First, this chapter discuss about the independent variable. This variable appears to be the major interest in our experiments. Next, the dependent variables. This variable will help us to measure participants’ behavior in response to the manipulation of the variable and it Is also important to identify the hypothesis in the experiments to see the nature of the relation between the dependent and independent variable. Furthermore, the book also defines the control a variable, a variable to control the circumstances in a way that to ensure that they do not vary from single level. In general, the random variable can enhance the external validity. In addition to the random variable, there is some circumstances where the random variable is limited by certain constraint, it is called random variable with certain constraints. In conjunction to the variables in an experiment, one should minimize the confounding variable to exist because confounding variable happens to be any circumstances that change systematically as the experimenter manipulates the independent variable.

 

Confounding variable can cause internal validity to happen. The threat might include the history, maturation, selection, mortality, testing, statistical regression and interaction selection in which all of these terms were comprehensively described in this chapter.

 

By understanding these definitions. I am now become more aware of how to design a good experiment for my research. Thus, after reading this chapter, I become more confident in designing some good experiments.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
MacKenzie Ch 4: Scientific Foundations (121-132)


This chapter provided a very useful review of the core concepts in research - it was an effective reminder for me of exactly how many facets I must take into account when considering a new idea or proposal for a research project; it is not only the originality or how interesting a concept is but also how well it fits into all of the considerations mentioned in the chapter that are very important factors to consider. One important concept I appreciated being emphasized was that the actual conduct of empirical research should always be based on observation and experience alone, without being biased by previous knowledge of theories, even if the research being conducted is relevant to a theory itself. Another was that research does not proceed in a vacuum, that much of it is incremental and not usually monumental.

items.name: 林奕汝
items.note: As a researcher, we can't have the whole user group to do experiments. It's always the question for me that how to convince people with such results generated from partial participants. A confidence interval will tell us the most likely range of the unknown population mean or proportion. In the section of How precise are our estimates_confidence intervals, we know the history of confidence intervals and the pros and cons of them. It also explained many confusing things like z as the critical value from the normal distribution (a 90% confidence level uses 1.64, a 95% confidence level uses 1.96 and a 99% confidence level uses 2.57). Also the mean or medium of result can't show how the data is distributed. The margins and standard errors are used to show more about the distribution. Representing the data in a sentence/figure is just like mapping the Earth on 2-D. Both of them lose some details and require researchers' good cares depending on where they want to focus.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
Sauro_CH3: How precise are our estimates? confidence intervals

In a research, it's too difficult to access to the entire population. We have to rely on taking samples to estimate the unknown population values but the estimate from a sample is not exactly right. A confidence interval is required, which provides both a measure of location and precision.

This chapter provides us with ways to know how precise our estimates are and how to computing confidence intervals for whether small or large sample size. For most researchers, "confidence interval" is a common sense. In addition, a number of different statistical software help us to analyze. However, we sometimes neglect the knowledge and history about confidence interval. The chapter promoted me to review these statistical concepts.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
How to do experiments

This chapter provides extensive definition of variable in an experiment. Once I did a physical experiment, “manipulated variable” and “controlled variable” were key words that I frequently met. Actually they are only a kind of variables called “independent variable” which is independent of the participant’s behavior. After reading this article, I realized that more details out of my mind have to be considered when doing an experiment. Because circumstances are highly changeable, experimenters should attempt to eliminate or minimize confounding variables that change systematically with the independent variable and distort the relationship between independent and dependent variables. When a circumstance is manipulated it also causes a change in behavior. Although we can ignore the other behaviors, we need to make sure we can account for all the circumstances. That’s why we need to be really careful when doing experiments.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
Martin_Chapter 2_How to do experiments

The chapter aims to introduce how to design a good experiment. In order to validate your hypothesis, we should take care of the variables, such as independent variable, dependent variable, control variable, and random variable, even deeply dig what the implicit confounding variable is in your experiment. 

According to your hypothesis, which is usually what you want to figure out, the independent variable and the dependent variable could be determined. The independent variable is manipulated by experimenters and independent of the participants' behavior. Conversely, the dependent variable is dependent on what the participants do. Through the relationship between the independent variable and dependent variable, we can propose non/directional hypothesis. Further considering other factors may affect the results of experiment, we also need to carefully setup the control variable and the random variable, which purpose is to generalize the findings in the real world. Otherwise, we need to know whether the manipulated change within the independent variable leads to the change in the dependent variable. This is the most important thing when we conduct a experiment. The chapter guides me how to design a experiment in the future.

items.name: 蔡守恩
items.note:
How to Do Experiments

Since high school education, we all know that designing an experiment needs only one variable and needs an experiment group and a control group. This is the most fundamental and I would easily deduce these to the psychology related experiments.

After reading, I must say, the original thought is not totally wrong, but it’s just too vague. One of my inspiration is that the complexity of human being inevitably poses numerous threats to experiments themselves (in the article it means internal validity and in spite of the inevitability, we still need to try our effort to decrease their influence). The author keeps warning us that we need to be very careful about these details when designing experiments, or the results are utterly useless. It builds the concepts that we must elaborately and logically plan. The whole is not as easy as I thought before; I’m too naïve.

However, I recalled the complains from one friend of mine who studies in the US. She usually voluntarily joins the psychology experiments in her college but she always got angry after experiments. “The purpose of testing is always not the thing they told you, they usually secretly observe another human characteristic,” she messaged. And this maps to the concepts that the author mentioned. It’s all for the precision and generalization of experiments.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
In most of the research, it is important to know the users. However, we are almost unable to get access to the entire user population, instead we can only sample more or less portion of the entire user population.

This chapter introduced the component of the confident intervals and formulas for different situations depending on the accuracy and population. The sample population affect the confidence interval largely (the confidence interval width and sample size have an inverse square root relationship), so it is concerned to consider the balance between sample size and accuracy.

After reading this chapter introducing the confidence interval, I reflect about the sample method, which means if there is criteria for the sample method, which can better sample the group that can describe the entire population as good as possible.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
How to make orderly observations

This book briefly discusses how to do experiments in the science of psychology. In the research for understanding human behavior, establishing relationships between circumstances and behaviors and fitting these relationships into an orderly body of knowledge are primary tasks. The relationship is always between a set of circumstances and a behavior, so it shows up the quantitative methods. On the other hand, qualitative researchers use descriptive data, such as written descriptions of people, including opinions and attitudes, and of events and environments.

 

Sometimes when an experimental approach cannot be used, it is necessary to use correlational observations, in which variables are observed and their relationships evaluated. The form of questionnaire or interview belongs to this method which is usually used in HCI research.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
How to make orderly observations

This reading gives an overview of psychological research methods. The purpose of doing psychological research is to find relationships between circumstances and behaviors and to fit relationships into orderly knowledge. The key awareness of doing psychological research is to consider human variability either among trials or among individuals. To handle the variability, we can use statistical techniques or control experiment as much as possible in research. This article then discuss quantitative and qualitative research. For each type of research, the author listed three methods. My main take aways from these methods are understanding (1) when and why to apply the method and (2) their advantages and disadvantages.

I really enjoy reading this article. Many of the HCI research methods apply from psychological research. As I systematically go through these concepts in psychological perspectives, I recall many of methodologies presented in HCI papers while reflecting on their pros and cons.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
How to make orderly observations

The author introduces several quantitative and qualitative methods from the aspect of psychology throughout the whole chapter. Although it is not the same as HCI, I think we can still learn a lot from such methods. The reading compares the different methods and indicate that we should use which method for which scenario. Moreover, the reading also reminds me that we should be careful about confounding variables when designing experimental method. I think it is very important and I was often negligent of considering it.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
How to do experiments

This reading interpret some important concepts about doing experiments for making casual statement. I learned more about factors that may harm internal validity. Before reading this article, I knew that we should minimize confounding variables, but limited to know types of possible confounding variables, such as history events, maturation of participants and statistical regression. I think it's helpful to keep these concepts as a check list and check it before I design an experiment in the future.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
Scientific Foundations

I appreciate the author share his perspective of doing research in an honest way a lot. I learned what is a HCI research question and I found new perspectives about "finding a HCI research topic", which is a challenging activity that I am facing. The author provides many useful and simple tips to this activity, and mostly encouraging us to find small problem from our experience or literature.
